Measles is one of the most contagious diseases in the world.

It’s also one of the most preventable.

As a doctor, let me be clear up front: Measles can’t be cured or prevented with Vitamin A or cod liver oil. The _only_ reliable way to stop its spread is through vaccination.

So it’s both frustrating and frightening when avoidable public health outbreaks like this occur:

---
This isn’t random. It’s the direct result of stripping away public health programs and funding that used to keep outbreaks like this from happening in the first place — and the dangerous and widespread disinformation about vaccines this administration spreads.

**Bottom line: the record-high measles outbreak happening in our country is the result of putting someone in charge of our public health infrastructure who doesn't understand medicine, and who actively undermines science and experts. **

I care deeply about public health as a physician, as a mom, and as a human being. And I know exactly what vaccine misinformation costs — not in dollars, but in people's lives.

Before the measles vaccine, hundreds of children used to die every year from measles, thousands were hospitalized, and many suffered lifelong consequences. This new outbreak has already tragically cost two unvaccinated school-aged children their lives.

We don’t have to go back to a time when kids were dying from a disease that modern medicine solved decades ago. We just need leaders who trust doctors and believe in science over conspiracy theories.

**I will continue fighting the disinformation coming from Trump and RFK Jr, and I could really use you by my side — because the more voices we can add to the chorus, the more likely it is we will make a real impact.**

Hey friend — Deb here.
I know my team and I have been emailing you a lot lately, but today I am reaching out personally to ask for your input: [**Will you be one of the _FIRST_ to join my official Healthcare Survey and share your thoughts with me?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16267?refcode=jtk1219-su-nd&code=jtk1219-su-nd&t=3&akid=11975%2E400544%2Exl2Zk0)

---
Attacks on healthcare are personal to me. I know what it feels like to wonder how you’ll afford a doctor’s appointment, stare down a medical bill you can’t pay, and rely on programs like Planned Parenthood, WIC, and Medicaid to make sure your family gets the care it needs.
Right now, accessible healthcare is under attack. Donald Trump’s policies are dismantling the healthcare system New Mexicans rely on. When his Medicaid cuts take effect in 2027, more than five rural hospitals could close, families could lose coverage, clinics could be forced to cut services, and healthcare workers could lose their jobs. For rural New Mexicans, that could mean driving hours for care that used to be available close to home.

_That’s why New Mexicans need a Governor who will stand up to this agenda, not help bring it here._

My Republican opponent will bring Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda to New Mexico. He’s taking his cues from Trump, who has already made life harder for New Mexicans by cutting healthcare, food assistance, and other programs families rely on. He won’t stand up to Trump or fight to protect these programs — _and he’s even promised to work with extremist Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to restrict reproductive healthcare._ **Meanwhile, I will fight to protect the healthcare New Mexicans rely on.**
As Governor, I’ll fight to protect reproductive freedom, lower healthcare costs, and make sure every New Mexican can get care close to home. But I’ve always believed that good leaders listen first. [**Friend, your perspective is critical to this campaign. Please take two minutes to share your healthcare priorities with me today.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16267?refcode=jtk1219-su-nd&code=jtk1219-su-nd&t=6&akid=11975%2E400544%2Exl2Zk0)

When his Medicaid cuts take effect in 2027, more than five rural hospitals could close, families could lose coverage, clinics could be forced to cut services, and healthcare workers could lose their jobs. For rural New Mexicans, that could mean driving hours for care that used to be available close to home. That’s why New Mexicans need a Governor who will stand up to this agenda, not help bring it here. My Republican opponent will bring Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda to New Mexico. He’s taking his cues from Trump, who has already made life harder for New Mexicans by cutting healthcare, food assistance, and other programs families rely on. He won’t stand up to Trump or fight to protect these programs — and he’s even promised to work with extremist Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to restrict reproductive healthcare. Meanwhile, I will fight to protect the healthcare New Mexicans rely on. As Governor, I’ll fight to protect reproductive freedom, lower healthcare costs, and make sure every New Mexican can get care close to home. But I’ve always believed that good leaders listen first. | | Thank you for your valuable input. – Deb | | | | | |

body:
Taking the fight to the next step

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/de2b1cd69aea/breaking-news-citizens-only-voting-amendment-submitted-to-board-of-canvassers-8371916?e=ecf60db114)

| | | | | [DONATE TODAY](https://us.list-manage.com/17qC0Vsf0ZT?e=ecf60db114&c2id=b020b7081f44f277164dc2a0d73e83a2)
---
|

| |

Dear Supporters,
Yesterday was a difficult and deeply disappointing day for Citizen Only Voting Michigan and for the more than 700,000 Michiganders who signed our petition.
Despite the evidence presented in support of certification, the Michigan Board of State Canvassers deadlocked on placing the Michigan Citizen Only Voting Amendment on the November 3 ballot.
Throughout this process, we have maintained that we have the signatures and that every valid petition signature deserves to be fairly considered. That principle became especially important in the cases of 23 Michigan voters who took the extraordinary additional step of submitting notarized affidavits confirming that they personally signed our petition.
Even then, five of those signatures were rejected despite Bureau of Elections staff and all four members of the Board acknowledging on the record that the individuals are registered Michigan voters and that the signatures on their affidavits match signatures contained in the Qualified Voter File.
Think about that for a moment.
These are registered voters who came forward personally, swore under oath that they signed our petition and provided signatures matching their official voter records. We believe that should represent the strongest possible confirmation that a voter signed a petition and intended for his or her voice to be heard.
We are deeply disappointed by the Board's deadlock, but yesterday's meeting does not end the legal process.
Because the Board was unable to certify the petition, we will now take this matter to the Michigan Supreme Court. There, we will continue to defend the validity of these petition signatures and the right of Michigan voters to have their signatures fairly considered.
However, taking this case to the Michigan Supreme Court will require significant legal resources. For those who wish to financially support the costs associated with this legal effort, contributions to Citizen Only Voting Michigan will help cover legal fees and other expenses related to the court proceedings.
Whatever happens next, we want you to know how grateful we are for everyone who has been part of this effort and gotten us this far. More than 700,000 Michiganders put their names on these petitions. Thousands more helped circulate petitions, collected signatures, attended events, contributed resources and followed this process every step of the way.
That extraordinary effort deserves to be recognized.
In the meantime, stay tuned. We will keep you informed as the case moves forward and will share developments as they happen. We will also share tools and resources to help us get our message out. We have the signatures and they should be fairly considered.
Thank you for standing with us and for everything you have done to bring Citizen Only Voting this far.
Sincerely,**Citizen Only Voting Michigan Team**
**P.S. If you can, please consider contributing $1, $5, $10, $25 or more, every dollar helps fund the upcoming legal battle!**

Hey Peter,

If you haven’t already, you’ll likely start seeing MAGA Republicans use my
full name a lot more in the coming weeks: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.

Donald Trump has already started using it as if it’s a punchline. ̄\_(
ツ)_/ ̄

Peter, I’ve
spent the majority of my career being someone who’s relatively young,
relatively brown, and relatively Muslim. Something I’ve learned along the
way is that when someone reaches for your name instead of your record,
it's because your record is the thing they can't touch:

* I’ve helped make government agencies actually work for Michiganders —
first by rebuilding Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy, and
then restructuring Wayne County’s Department of Health, Human &
Veterans Services.
* As a public servant, I’ve removed lead from elementary schools, taken
on Michigan’s biggest polluters, and made life-saving Narcan
universally accessible.

There’s nothing for them to attack there — so that’s why they’re resorting
to a politics rooted in hatred instead.

Meanwhile, Mike Rogers has a record he'd rather Michiganders never look at
too closely:

* Mike Rogers voted to raise his own pay in Congress.
* He championed a bill that helped create the opioid crisis.
* Then, after spending 15 years in Washington, he left and got $14
million richer working for the very corporations he used to regulate,
then moved to Florida.

And that’s why Mike Rogers needs $51,000,000+ worth of help to have a
chance at beating us in November.

We’re never going to outraise $51 million, but we don’t have to. We just
need folks to pitch in $10 to help us respond to their
attacks and get our message in front of as many Michiganders as possible.
If we do that, we will win. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260825-3-ak.o_RUNe&amount=10&refcode=em20260825-3014&t=1004&akid=3020%2E251025%2EKAY9m0 ]Can I count on your support,
Peter?

In solidarity,

Abdul

| | | I sat down with _New York Times_ columnist Ezra Klein for one of the longest interviews I've ever done.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137923915/642426384/724950626?refcode=260825-ezraklein-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZTVkNjFkZC1mMWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=agDMiIlDPQFeSQYl0zqhERZzuXWmOsRP6OAEqyhDxCA=)
---
It's been a funny experience. People suddenly seem fascinated by this idea that an auto repair and machine shop owner from Skamania County wound up in Congress. _But honestly... I'm not sure I'm all that interesting._ I still wake up in the same house, work at the same shop with my husband, and struggle to find child care. I still worry about whether small businesses can survive. I still believe if the government writes a rule that doesn't make sense, we ought to fix it. The cameras leave. The work continues. Sometimes I think Washington, D.C. forgets that. Politics has become so focused on the next headline that we've stopped asking whether anything actually works. I didn't run for Congress because I wanted to become famous. **I ran for office because I got tired of watching practical problems pile up while everyone argued about them.** That's why I'm still in this fight. _If more people are paying attention now, I hope they're paying attention to that._ Because Congress doesn't need more personalities. It needs more people willing to roll up their sleeves. **[If you think so too, I could use your support. Please chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can afford to help me keep working away at the clunker that is DC.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137923916/642426385/724950626?refcode=260825-ezraklein-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZTVkNjFkZC1mMWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=agDMiIlDPQFeSQYl0zqhERZzuXWmOsRP6OAEqyhDxCA=) **

We got word about a brand-new poll here in North Carolina, and it’s not
looking good:

Following the millions of dollars the GOP has been pouring into attack ads
against me, a brand-new poll out last week that shows Michael Whatley and
I are statistically tied. If that’s all you need to hear today, please use
this link to split a donation between our campaign and Chris Pappas and
stop them from taking the lead:

this seat, we’ll lose our chance at taking back the U.S. Senate majority.

This new poll only confirms what we’ve known all along: this is going to

I’ve been a top target for national Republicans all cycle. So far, GOP

Fellow Patriot -

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

_**I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator,[who is humbly asking for your support.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=f8058d593b49445ca3376330cb469d98&_e=ckym_QkG6SZfZ4AuLlXUkcSNVpMlVeJUXA3QKjqvi2moMJaO64VEylRl0otCmnRjllE6t3b0-rkV_erGNKRAofysTqmKm0-ZiHZL4Ld3jOM33zcSQ0T4sRF0cXXW4V3eAIse8iZlGjz7zdvG_1FPNxms5uTmxc18rthnEMXzqfHBpIR1-v7H98blKCfa_pWqVrXeRJwSa4WVaZvyDOtTNWnLP9ihgt-cqc5scYYo7-566UJ7266D7YsXSzBCME-p_M_HNsW9XmL2S00hhjg76sflclZmSUBA18YOBU10haVaCz-CPo28Zze6l5SB10MTRbCrEPiNbym7GL5rS3lQguT5KcPeDpP7pHPwKzX0k0cH4Vca0u9dhsqWX470H37CWHb85RfgM62mTJqFjbgpf_lsGQq8pWUUL7iBxPJdftvdJQujp-zhRidVNZFbkUtbuwyRCuBQp9e6cCsXbu4O4Ms02FBB3VW4FZKLc8MgMeVoFsBs2guv4sCw_fHfsyKGmUYnvcu9Ws1XEdHiATtfSR6BgDuHzi02XL0FChn69Hf2DODv-ReCStxf4d2MjfHZDJBqNBuCwMVHqfPCOH8cRRbAHu_484yUu-700vnAsWhZRI67siRQVsR3iEWMR54OoxsV0aQk4UlvueN0X2Gzn5Ep74PyCGKrj_sFi1H0IGKCpPR6KM0DMr9fVnhLN75tJKHDxEFxH4zAvL-ozznyFA9BVzGLAbCCVVSIsJv7649RwMDE6UPbWjYngAOIBEEQw1svDCY5hKHft5YcS6IspQ%3D%3D)**_

I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater.

I support the Right to Life.
I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country.
I oppose DEI.
I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y.
I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions.
I stand for the national anthem.
I believe our veterans are heroes.
I will always Back the Blue.
**And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again.**
I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. _**My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second.**_

clean_body: I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. | Peter - I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country. I oppose DEI. I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y. I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions. I stand for the national anthem. I believe our veterans are heroes. I will always Back the Blue. And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second. She supports turning confused little boys into little girls and vice versa. name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Greg Ballard’s $2.5 Million Voter Guide Plan Is Redundant Government Waste
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
INGOP Press Release No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** August 25, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, **[kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)****Greg Ballard's $2.5 Million Voter Guide Plan Is Redundant Government Waste****Indianapolis, IN** - Greg Ballard is proposing a taxpayer-funded voter guide that would be mailed to every registered Indiana voter before each general election, along with a companion smartphone app.There's just one problem: Indiana already provides many of these services.Hoosiers already have access to statewide voter information, candidate lists and personalized ballot information through the Secretary of State's office and IndianaVoters.com. Nonprofit organizations also work to provide voters with election information and resources.Instead of working with nonprofits already providing voter resources or improving the services Indiana already has, Ballard's solution is to balloon state government with another taxpayer-funded program, which he says would cost an average of $2.5 million per year. Despite the $2.5 million annual price tag, Ballard has yet to provide a detailed budget explaining how it would be implemented, funded or sustained.Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling said Ballard's proposal reflects a broader problem with his campaign: proposing new government programs without explaining what they would cost or whether they are necessary. "Greg Ballard is touting a 'first-of-its-kind' voter guide, but there's nothing innovative about asking Hoosier taxpayers to fund services Indiana already provides."Instead of finding ways to improve existing resources or work with organizations already doing this work, Ballard's answer is more government and more spending, without even providing Hoosiers a detailed budget for how he plans to pay for it."This is becoming a pattern. Greg Ballard and Beau Bayh are campaigning on big promises without explaining whether the Secretary of State's office can actually deliver them. Hoosiers deserve more than campaign promises. They deserve a Secretary of State who understands the office, respects their hard-earned tax dollars and makes government work better, not bigger."### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. body:
Ten days ago, I laced up my shoes at Rock's Diner in Fort Kent, and started walking south. I told myself I would listen first and talk second.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter, Ten days ago, I laced up my shoes at Rock's Diner in Fort Kent, and started walking south. I told myself I would listen first and talk second. That is exactly what we've been doing. The **For a Better Maine Tour** has brought us from **Fort Kent, Madawaska, Caribou, and Presque Isle** down through **Medway, Millinocket, East Millinocket, Old Town, Orono, and Skowhegan** \- and the response has changed this campaign. [Check out NewsCenter Maine's news coverage from my ](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=0ZEw3rKCYdU6QDR4jANpCzJgPR1oXz7mjSdU-TTQM5knkPQwhnwTMNs7BsVzdgJm4p_34enJRePYZ0wlFFId4hAeQf-xzfr02ivWd9TJNvj2XTZfledmTiHAtu4EFqBLYniveboMpeDcctldILlC39Yn1Q4KYdWz4AjuNpwnz7Ew_VG0qWtHHpOIg7AvMpQzI9NznGUnEuqThoiTYqVlEHAjPL-1RAD-TwRflwsp0cQkz63QF4NScV98_uGihJbc&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=1)time in Skowhegan. What I’m experiencing on the ground is not what you'll see in a poll or a political ad. It's Mainers sitting with me in diner booths and chatting in hardware stores – sharing that they can't afford to live here anymore. It's young people at UMaine wondering whether they can build a life in the state they grew up in. It's small business owners telling me exactly which budget line is going to determine whether they make it to another year. That is what this campaign is about. Not a slogan. **A conversation.** I am running as an **independent** , free of the party bosses in DC and Augusta, and that is landing differently on a porch in [Millinocket than it does in a TV ad](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=0ZEw3rKCYdU6QDR4jANpCzJgPR1oXz7mjSdU-TTQM5knkPQwhnwTMNs7BsVzdgJm4p_34enJRePYZ0wlFFId4hAeQf-xzfr02ivWd9TJNvj2XTZfledmTiHAtu4EFqBLYniveboMpeDcctldILlC39Yn1Q4KYdWz4AjuNpwnz7Ew_VG0qWtHHpOIg7AvMpQzI9NznGUnEuqThoiTYqVlEHAjPL-1RAD-TwRflwsp0cQkz63QF4NScV98_uGihJbc&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=2). People are tired of being told who to vote for. They are ready to be asked what they actually need. But here's the truth: an independent campaign runs on direct support from folks like you -- not DC party bosses or dark money special interest groups. Every mile of road I've walked, every diner stop, every ride from a volunteer is powered by donors like you. The walking tour is working because of you. To keep this momentum going through the fall, we need to fund the next stretch of the road - more nights in small towns, more travel, more listening, more signs on more Mainers' lawns. **Will you chip in today to keep the For a Better Maine tour and our independent campaign moving?**

What I’m experiencing on the ground is not what you'll see in a poll or a political ad. It's Mainers sitting with me in diner booths and chatting in hardware stores – sharing that they can't afford to live here anymore. It's young people at UMaine wondering whether they can build a life in the state they grew up in. It's small business owners telling me exactly which budget line is going to determine whether they make it to another year. That is what this campaign is about. Not a slogan. A conversation. I am running as an independent , free of the party bosses in DC and Augusta, and that is landing differently on a porch in . People are tired of being told who to vote for. But here's the truth: an independent campaign runs on direct support from folks like you -- not DC party bosses or dark money special interest groups. Every mile of road I've walked, every diner stop, every ride from a volunteer is powered by donors like you. The walking tour is working because of you. ## Dolly Parton Dies at 80
Dolly Parton, the Grammy-winning singer, songwriter, and actress whose [larger-than-life persona and six-decade](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAQBeDTmM7IDH-mcJGGbtOmRF48ZicyeGXPQrh9xOYI6UYa6T197-s23SwF2pZPu6JhH6cNjxyQGdPkYgjn0yaOmyPMPpy0LWx_aAIFnVRaQjfZmWnHqbGFMx4RsC7QVL3u-1pr3RYPY_W9UrZT3ul73bTe9z22XoOehwEGpQsyV57S0FVKadWU0NbYOu_A-6FybS0ahY44pvI70sYP9OGMO6ZyjmsRzIP5mUX9IWAUMB7HUc73fDmuv4DxOgWMb47888gLJO2CUis5x9fG6ZTrK9MsM9skYCyScc-DQqDc9aJRy2opvAv5nzvtBn4DAAD__wpgfsA) career made her one of America's most beloved entertainers, died peacefully at her Nashville home, her family announced Tuesday. She was 80. The fourth of 12 children raised in rural Tennessee, Parton sold over [100 million records](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uAjEQxfHT2N0ie_y5hYs0dKRNaVnMGCYy69WuBeH2EeQIqZ_0l37v65RPhRsvl89yozRqzws99kZj0Jaxt_Zcyzb6gkx7bU9eLqP8cAYFflJxAp_LefCdsi0SUyUCMpKSDjEEE2N08ppK0DoAKWdnH4NCmE0o1jjUszVwdpLTq6cieK1UVPYAzpDDilDrrNEZYRUhj74dvjsv40q1PfudtsO532RL1zHWXZgPAUcBx5X62ug1CTi-CdOfYUIqOAXnXXRGbgnXB7fGuw_CqsutcHv3xj9vuCf4DQAA__8mxXDr) on the strength of hits like _Jolene_ and _I Will Always Love You_ , starred in the hit movie _9 to 5_ ,__ and built Dollywood into one of the country's most-visited theme parks. Parton was an inspirational figure to many, often focusing on forgiveness and prayer in interviews. President Trump [ordered all American flags flown at half-mast](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQxvGnMZ0jMxgwhYtr6HLtlcjBY5jbASM8m2zefpXsI2z9SX_p9_27TtdATPvyN2zoJeVpx0dhFMFzipn5eYRT8h4JS-In7YuEL5rAQKeN09BNYRa642RDFX1CBGwq9HXv-r5xzrXV6m2oU-8s2mZuAefhNjQGhxbmcJttaE1F_tUzDrraGGfsBdoG25gipDTUsW2UNRhJ8nn5n2mXFRM_8x3Py5y3iv0qchTV_FEwKhhlxZWYX5uC8cZ5KQpG2rWsqD_2_FAwdsYOQ13rt1D_ELWcn9uhE4el6DVw0kVCSgrG6vTxeBAzla5X1ixboHe_kl9edvfwHQAA__8KZYGb) for a week, saying, _"There has never been anyone like her, and never will."_ She had faced health setbacks following the death of her husband Carl Dean in March 2025 and canceled a planned Las Vegas residency. Her family asked for donations to the [Imagination Library](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz7FuwjAQgOGnSTaQudiJGTx0YaNrR-vIncNVjo2cEzRvX9FX6P7rk_6va7yiZCnLJ64cNNVY-LVlVuUWqea8P7BpLSS8pbxLWRR_JIKB8WD8AcaIs8qTo8WeQmIGHnoOp8lP0-C9d_09INvZzoDWk0NjHU5null3my0RDyP2Et6e8TCejPHGHsEN7CgRpHQ-kRs6a5hEazt-Vyl655T3-uR2nOva53BXfWzd8NHBpYOLrLhIQZVastwatv2ddXDpW6DHS3KWbZw6a5YVJf8R-s_zZ4DfAAAA__-QiG95) in lieu of flowers. ## Canada Hits Back with 50% Tariffs
Canada struck back Tuesday, announcing [retaliatory tariffs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unTAQBOCnMR3ILH-mcJGG7qRNiRZ2fXBkbGQ2h_D2V9xXuN1II30jzZ_X_EIffHz_xp2tuDRHvs7AIpxnSiHcB2ZJkTyfLtw-vgX_-xk09KU2JfQzruI_PLdYkHXMwE3Bth7MMDTGmK7Y7LhA1w84LgR1rZ3hgWkkXsZlbJCAC28fTxvoa62NbivoGu7IETg31tQ1qtVMXlKu_iYfZWMX7vThXK1pL4LdRI5TNb8UTAqm67qqNS7rUyqYHlrBpM2TOwXTihEJS8n_9qMUzN65s5SMxOWKOfJdBl4CxrXaZA9FtnRcPgR_9oNq9XtHH7535Yd3fSx8BQAA___1hIAa) as high as 50% on more than 700 American products, matching President Trump's newest levies "dollar for dollar."

The counter-tariffs cover about $20 billion in U.S. goods, from steel and dairy to appliances, and take effect Sept. 8. The move came after weekend talks collapsed and a fresh round of 50% U.S. tariffs took effect Saturday. Trump has since [vowed to double](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp8Gd6ww-AcXFIkidzdtSmvWDPasMFgwuxu_fbR5hVt_0qdzzp-v5QsoUtp-w4GOQ14SvmtEZiyLzzFeJxTOyRPWEC9KG8NfWrTSg1RW6mGBlemFSweNdwFRo2nQtaMdR2Ot7Zvd9X4AmOxkOwsqdAFMp8zQtvce1tVq35D7_Cmrh1Ypq7qb7g32PngdwtT63ohOoSfO5fbIlHjHEK_8wnJb89FEtzOfVZgfQs9Cz3BfPw6fTej557NSwlqFnrk8j1PuGKOk48wVZcK3ZCgUQpUrJPAgH5CeUC6JdYUITGkTeq6cyyXMTF6YX63pJ9XqaWyK8-ebYqQ6jKJT2wEU_yPxN0u-nP4XAAD__4AZig4) tariffs on Canadian cars, steel, and trucks in January. Trump responded on Truth Social, threatening to [rename Lake Ontario](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU9jOpA9gPEWLtLQbdqUyOAxTGJsZCa74fbR5grpfvH19PQ-7tPdUaS0vrsdLYc8JXyeEZmxTD7HeB2ucE6e8AzxorSy-6EJJOhamhr05BamB06dq7wNiIBthVYNZhhaY0xfbVbpAZcZ5lliP4PTShutbt7r26Ba7HVF9sWTBrSS0siugb7F3gcPIdyU71vRSfTEuTSfmRJvGOKVH1iaJe9VtBvzcYr2TcAoYAyUXFqwudyW8-shYMQlp7xfAsYjR1pewxWmJeIpYOTyvR81XnjWBZPbKa11dF9Y58SuUK6VaodeKyWbjfdYFeuPJ8VIpx5EJ9fdUfxT4X8WfFj4DQAA__8MPIdR) "Lake America," saying the U.S. doesn't expect to do "much business with Ontario any longer."
## Study: 1 in 4 Deceased NFL Players Had CTE
At least one in four former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), and the true rate could be as high as 97.7%, according to a [study published](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQxfHTmMzIlDEfgYNNyHrTDZHB5carahvhGhhuP-q-wsQ_6enp_-8xP1ykmJ5_3QsthzwnvAohMx6zz0T37g7OyUcsge6Ynuy-4wwKOqkGCd3sVo4nzq2rvA2IgLpC2_RD3-thGEy1WdfpZVxWrXVwi_HGOwULrkqPYQ3ahSra954aoGuUGlRbg9FofPAQwth4o0Wr0EfOR_0_x8QbBrrziUe95ldFdmPei9B_BEwCpuu6aix7eqOAKQUSMBXOxy1gmgVM0QuY2rGHpjHdx778LcuWryIJXWEJRqZAcid341GkxxMp73JlrA7r9ysSxdL1olXPl4v0ucG_rHda-AkAAP__D1GFiw) in _The British Medical Journal_. The findings land just as football season is about to kick off across America. The study tracked 1,712 former players who died between 2008 and 2021. Of the 338 who [donated their brains](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpCAURb8Gd1TwIYgLFpNMzGxqtr006HuUr4NikFS1f9-p_oVe3-TmnPNxn-6BE--P_2EjX2OednqdiWqlMmFO6TpCqXlHpjOmi_dHDV88gQIrlZNgp7BUftLUhQZ9JALSDfm2d32vnXOmWb2Kg221no1eYMDZ9joMvV1ii4PDxcwN-_efcmBbpZzqbmA0GYwIMQ4tGi06Rcg1l9tn5r2uFNOVn1RuS96a5Ndaj1PoPwJGAWOYl7fDexMw_qOQ6ipgbGUnYy4bFbnHJI8ULiqnRCaUF4UiDyqcUcB41lwuoUdGof-22gxada5risfjxSnxaXvRqccWOP0A1F92e3r4DgAA__8Ke4IR), 93.2% were diagnosed with CTE, and nearly 60% of those donors had dementia. By comparison, CTE appears in [less than 1%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQQNHTmM5oGBvwFi7S0G3alMjg8eLIYGRml3D7aHOFXOA_6X_dx7uLKW6PT7eS5ZDHjc4jETOV0eeUrt0VzpuPdIR0xe3B7ieOCNhJMBK70c0cXzRqV3kbiJBURbbpTd8rY0xbLVYDTLd-Cgp0AwBdq5Vxqsfb7GHSXlfRvntgsGsADOgaW0WtDx5DuDW-VUID-ci51N85brxQSFd-UannvFbJLsz7IdSHwEHgcJ5nPT1r8k-Bgysc50SHwOFtCBxWt10y5LJSkVtIck_uonLIxXk5M8mJQi4kPTleqmL9fsaU4tH1QsNjdTH9ofzPVy-LvwEAAP__wHl-yg) of the general population. Most players in the study competed before 2005, when the disease was first identified in an NFL player, so recent safety reforms may not be reflected in the data.

It is already that time.
The midterm elections are not even here yet. We have no idea who will control the House or Senate. But apparently, it is time to start speculating about who will run for president in 2028
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57cbad56-c47e-4b8a-b29b-21df1a501128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I want to start with the Republicans.
I am ranking the potential candidates from D tier to S tier, with D being the worst and S sitting above A as the best. I am judging them on four basic questions:
Can they win a Republican primary? Can they defeat the Democratic nominee? Can they build and finance a national campaign? Do they have the charisma and media skills required to run for president?
Those categories are weighted evenly because this is not scientific. It is speculation, and, well... who the hell knows.
But I am going to do it anyway.
* * *
## D Tier
### Josh Hawley
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d6e20ec-ad33-45ce-b997-d00aac1e5f93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Josh Hawley has national name recognition. He is a sitting senator, reasonably telegenic and capable of raising money.
But I do not think he has the political power or charisma to break through a serious Republican presidential primary.
Hawley is still the guy who raised his fist toward protesters outside the Capitol on January 6 and was later shown running through the Capitol as the attack unfolded. Fairly or unfairly, that image made him look like a little bitch to a lot of people.
He may believe being an incumbent senator gives him enough clout to run. Incumbents normally win reelection, and senators naturally begin imagining themselves as presidents.
I do not see it.
More likely, Hawley positions himself for a future cabinet appointment or uses a presidential campaign to increase his influence within the party.
That puts him in D tier.
* * *
### Tim Scott
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0e4d4f-4494-4a9e-b60f-b9b7471f3555?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tim Scott has more political connections than people give him credit for. He can raise money, and he knows how to move around a debate stage without completely embarrassing himself.
I simply do not think he projects the political backbone people expect from a presidential candidate. He does not come across as somebody who will take control of the party, define the race and make voters believe he should be president.
He has connections. He has donors. He has experience.
I do not think he has the gumption.
D tier.
* * *
### Vivek Ramaswamy
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c5adffd5-87e3-4302-8b5e-7454087c015c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Vivek Ramaswamy created plenty of attention during the 2024 Republican primary. That campaign helped him get selected to help lead the original Department of Government Efficiency effort with Elon Musk, although he "left" before the project formally began.
He is now the Republican nominee for governor of Ohio.
Vivek has money, national recognition and media skills. But I think the more people get to know him, the less they like him. He was passed over for the U.S. Senate appointment, passed over for vice president and never received a Senate-confirmed cabinet position. No one wants him anywhere.
Now he is running for governor.
If he wins and immediately turns around to run for president, people are going to ask why he wanted the governor's office in the first place. Ohioans would have every right to tell him to stay here and do the damn job.
If he loses the governor's race, that creates a different problem for a presidential campaign.
Either way, I have him in D tier.
* * *
### Pete Hegseth
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9350e2f3-e4cd-4daa-aa01-d477a4390735?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pete Hegseth is currently the secretary of defense, and his recent political travel to Iowa has already [generated speculation about a possible 2028 campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/d43ce735-3b57-40d1-8e4d-06ebab957be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I do not know where Hegseth's political future goes.
I could see him trying to stay in Republican politics, campaigning for other candidates or positioning himself for another administration job. I could even see his name being floated as a running mate.
But as a presidential candidate, I do not see a strong fundraising organization, broad coalition or convincing general-election profile.
People are talking about him, so he belongs on the list.
He also belongs in D tier.
* * *
## C Tier
### Sarah Huckabee Sanders
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5199f713-6d9a-4e5d-9912-05d15ccff112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sarah Huckabee Sanders is a loyal Trump ally, the governor of Arkansas and a known national figure because of her time as White House press secretary.
I considered putting her in B tier.
She could raise a respectable amount of money. She has political connections, and I think some moderate Republicans could convince themselves that she offers a calmer version of Trump's politics.
She has also clearly been working on her presentation and political profile as governor.
But I still do not think she generates enough excitement or has enough charisma to take control of a national primary.
My reaction is basically: meh.
That puts her in C tier.
* * *
### Greg Abbott
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e856c8b-2c31-4749-87af-1807d77c7a9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Greg Abbott is a powerful Republican governor with national name recognition and deep connections inside the party.
But I do not think he has the charisma to win a presidential campaign.
American presidential politics is also obviously ableist. Voters and the media tend to favor candidates who are taller, conventionally attractive and physically commanding on television. Abbott's use of a wheelchair should not affect his qualifications, but I think the political system would unfairly make it part of the campaign.
Even beyond that, I do not think he has the presence to take over a crowded Republican field.
C tier.
* * *
### Tulsi Gabbard
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4817c317-b471-4e20-b89a-f891e2854fc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tulsi Gabbard is an odd political figure.
She was a Democratic member of Congress and a Democratic presidential candidate. She became a Republican, joined Trump's administration as director of national intelligence and resigned in 2026, publicly citing her husband's serious health problems.
I still wonder whether leaving the administration also preserves her ability to begin preparing for 2028.
Tulsi has charisma. She has a strong media presence. She can raise money, and she would probably perform well on a debate stage.
**Her problem is trust.**
Many Republicans still do not trust her because she spent years as a prominent Democrat. Democrats do not trust her because she joined Trump and became a Republican.
That leaves her in a strange political limbo.
I could imagine her fitting into some kind of Tucker Carlson or Marjorie Taylor Greene political movement. I could even imagine a third-party campaign designed to disrupt the general election.
As the Republican nominee, though, I do not see it.
C tier.
* * *
### Byron Donalds
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f249f839-a6d9-4244-9ec2-c8d7d852df0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Byron Donalds just won the Republican nomination for governor of Florida. He will face former Republican congressman and now Democrat David Jolly in the November general election.
Donalds is generally liked within the Republican Party. Like Gabbard and Ramaswamy, he was previously a Democrat, but he does not carry the same political baggage from that transition.
He can raise money. He is comfortable on television, and I think he would perform well on a presidential debate stage.
His problem is timing.
If Donalds wins the governorship and immediately begins campaigning for president, Florida voters may reasonably ask why he ran for governor. If you win the job, do the job.
Would he really leave the Florida governor's office for a cabinet appointment? I would not.
He has potential, but 2028 may be too soon.
C tier.
* * *
## B Tier...
